title: Winter Is Past: The Eyes That Saw
summary: The vessel has been formed, and within that formed vessel the soul's eyes first open. Sight is given before any seeking begins; the divine is already interior to the materials gathered, and the soul tastes what was planted there. From this first opening the long work of recognition can begin. This is the threshold, and a threshold can be occupied by no more than one moment.
organizing_principle: A single teaching, because the state itself is a single moment — the first opening of sight after the self has been formed. The chapter is fragmentary; most of the surface is broken, but the surviving line is exact for what this moment is: the natural mind is shaped, the divine is already interior to the materials gathered, and the soul tastes from the perception planted in the formed vessel; its eyes look out. Everything that follows is the soul beginning to sort what these now-open eyes see.
